newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FINMIN APPROVES ELECTRICITY PRICE RISE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FINMIN APPROVES ELECTRICITY PRICE RISE.

text.p: The Czech Finance Ministry on Tuesday said it had approved a 15 percent rise in household electricity prices effective July 1.
"(The rise) returns to the originally proposed 15 percent increase," ministry spokeswoman Ludmila Nutilova told Reuters.

She added that with an expected rise in the value-added tax (VAT) to 22 percent from a current five percent, household prices for electricity in the Czech Republic should rise by just under 35 percent.
The Finance Ministry has the power to set electricity prices on its own, but parliament must still approve the raising of the VAT.
If it does approve the measure, the VAT increase would be effective as of January 1, 1998.
Two weeks ago, the government approved a global agreement on raising electrcity and natural gas prices, as well as rents, though some details are still being worked out.

Many Czechs still live in flats with artificially low rents and with energy bills subsidised by industrial users. This has made deregulation one of the stickiest political issues in the Czech Republic.

Economists have said the price deregulation moves could add several percentage points to the inflation rate but also suppress high levels of domestic demand, which are conbtributing to a widening trade gap.
Czech consumer prices rose 0.3 percent in February for a year-on-year rise of 7.3 percent, compared with an 8.8 average rise in 1996.
The trade deficit for the first two months of the year was 27.2 billion crowns, up from 16.2 billion crowns for the same period of the previous year.
